set.approach: Reach the Joint Wall from the third highway pullout toward Gold River by hiking down the trail into the rocky river bed, or from the Crest Lake day-use area. The route shares its start with Above All Splendour, the right-most line on the wall, and then follows bolts to the left.

set.approach: Reach the Joint Wall from the Crest Lake day-use area by taking the trail past the picnic tables and bearing left at the fork, or from the third highway pullout toward Gold River by hiking down into the rocky river bed. The route is the right-most line on the wall, beginning on an arete a little beyond the tree line.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchors at either belay.

set.approach: Drive the Kookipi Creek forest road to Branch 400 and follow it to the end of the usable road. From there bushwhack straight up into the alpine boulder field and keep climbing, skirting the foot of several big walls, to a huge face. The line begins at the face's left extreme, on splitter cracks.
set.descent_text: Follow the dirt gully down and west to a notch heading a gully that returns to the foot of the climb.

review.notes: Single-source facts from the route page and the crag page; counts left out unless two pages agree.

set.approach: From the old parking area, duck through the slide-alder tunnel that was once road 610. After a short walk you reach a stream bed below a big slab. The usual line stays on the road until it is opposite Steinbok Peak's prow, then drops down the stream, crosses it and follows a strip of old-growth forest up to the talus beneath the peaks. The first pitch sits above and to the left of the orange ramp that served as the original start, in a corner facing right; one bolt and a bouldery move identify it.
set.descent_text: Rappel down the waterfall gully that lies between Les Cornes and Ibex. The summit connects by a knife edge to the first rappel station, and the rappel stations in the gully have fixed nuts, slung blocks and trees.

set.approach: From the forest road off Highway 99 between Pemberton and Lillooet, park at the overgrown spur road. Hike up the old spur, crossing the first washed-out creek on a log, and where the road disappears into brush take the flagged, cairned climbers' trail uphill on the right. It runs alongside North Joffre Creek over boulders and alder, then drops to the creek's edge. Cross the creek when nearly below Mouse's Tooth and climb boulder fields to the foot of the left arete, with a large gully on its left.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route with two ropes. Bolted anchors are on every pitch but the fourth.

set.approach: From the forest road off Highway 99 between Pemberton and Lillooet, park at the overgrown spur road and follow the flagged climbers' trail beside North Joffre Creek to the base of Mouse's Tooth, as for Mighty Mouse. The route begins by taking Mighty Mouse's opening two pitches up to the large ledge, then traverses right through a hanging garden to a hanging ledge below a steep, dirty corner.

set.approach: Starting at the camp below Mount Gimli's south face, take the trail to the col between Gimli and Nisleheim. The route heads up the ramp to the east shoulder, then steps out onto the exposed north face.
set.descent_text: Rappel the south face with double ropes, or scramble down the northwest ridge at class 4, or reverse the route with one steep rappel down the first pitch to the ramp.

set.approach: Phyllis' Engine is a group of granite spires along the crest linking Mt Carr and Castle Towers. From the Sphinx (Burton) Hut on the southeast side of Garibaldi Lake, climb glaciated terrain to the ridge. Climb the scree gully along the Engine's north side, then drop down on the east side and mantle a couple of large blocks to a small belay nook, which is the start.
set.descent_text: Descend by the standard rappel route.
